lists the item's Chart images, from the edit\npage, and puts one in the body with a description; the server reads it back\nas `![Description](image:<name>)` (app.markdown_form), as T10/T11 store it.\nWhat the Editor does in the browser is checked by hand (the closing comment);\nhere, what the server gives it and what a post of its HTML saves.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport re\nfrom html import unescape\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom tests.test_t03_data_bites import create_bite\nfrom tests.test_t04_reports import create_report\nfrom tests.test_t10_chart_images import CHART, img_tags, png\nfrom tests.test_t10_chart_images import upload as upload_to_bite\nfrom tests.test_t11_report_chart_images import upload as upload_to_report\nfrom tests.test_t12_site_preview import preview\nfrom tests.test_t13_editor_routes import edit_page, editor_content, save, stored\n\nKINDS = [pytest.param(\"data-bites\", create_bite, upload_to_bite, id=\"data-bite\"),\n         pytest.param(\"reports\", create_report, upload_to_report, id=\"report\")]\n\n\ndef body_images(page: str) -> list[dict] | None:\n    \"\"\"The Chart images the page's Editor may insert; None if it is given\n    none to list, as on a create page.\"\"\"\n    found = re.findall(r\"\"\"<div class=\"admin-editor\"[^>]*? data-images='([^']*)'\"\"\", page)\n    return json.loads(unescape(found[0])) if found else None\n\n\ndef img(kind: str, item_id: str, name: str, alt: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A chart image as the Editor shows and posts it: from the admin route.\"\"\"\n    return f'<img src=\"/admin/{kind}/{item_id}/images/{name}\" alt=\"{alt}\">'\n\n\ndef module_for(kind: str):\n    from app import data_bites, reports\n    return data_bites if kind == \"data-bites\" else reports\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef analyst(client_as) -> TestClient:\n    return client_as(\"editor\")\n\n\n# What the Editor is given.\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"kind, create, upload\", KINDS)\ndef test_the_edit_page_gives_the_editor_its_chart_images_by_name_and_admin_src(\n        analyst, kind, create, upload):\n    item_id = create(analyst)\n    assert body_images(edit_page(analyst, kind, item_id)) == []\n\n    upload(analyst, item_id, png(\"spring.png\"))\n    upload(analyst, item_id, png(\"fall-by-class.png\"))\n    images = body_images(edit_page(analyst, kind, item_id))\n    assert images == [\n        {\"name\": \"fall-by-class.png\", \"src\": f\"/admin/{kind}/{item_id}/images/fall-by-class.png\"},\n        {\"name\": \"spring.png\", \"src\": f\"/admin/{kind}/{item_id}/images/spring.png\"}]\n    # Each src is the thumbnail the Editor shows, served to a signed-in user.\n    assert analyst.get(images[0][\"src\"]).content == png()[1]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"kind, create, upload\", KINDS)\ndef test_a_create_page_gives_the_editor_no_images_to_list(analyst, kind, create, upload):\n    page = analyst.get(f\"/admin/{kind}\").text\n    assert 'class=\"admin-editor\"' in page\n    assert body_images(page) is None\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"kind, create, upload\", KINDS)\ndef test_the_copy_a_snippet_list_is_gone_but_each_image_can_still_be_deleted(\n        analyst, kind, create, upload):\n    item_id = create(analyst)\n    upload(analyst, item_id, png())\n    page = edit_page(analyst, kind, item_id)\n    section = page[page.index('<section class=\"content-images\"'):]\n    assert \"![Description](image:\" not in page\n    assert \"fall-by-class.png\" in section\n    assert f'action=\"/admin/{kind}/{item_id}/images/fall-by-class.png/delete\"' in section\n    assert \"Insert image\" in section\n\n\n# What an insert, a change, or a removal saves.\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"kind, create, upload\", KINDS)\ndef test_an_inserted_image_is_stored_as_its_image_reference(analyst, kind, create, upload):\n    item_id = create(analyst, body=\"Enrollment by class:\")\n    upload(analyst, item_id, png())\n    page = edit_page(analyst, kind, item_id)\n\n    # As the Editor places it: a paragraph of its own after the cursor's.\n    html = (editor_content(page)\n            + f'<p>{img(kind, item_id, \"fall-by-class.png\", \"Fall enrollment by class\")}</p>'\n            + \"<p>Source: IR.</p>\")\n    assert save(analyst, kind, item_id, page, body_html=html, body_dirty=\"1\").status_code == 303\n    assert stored(module_for(kind), item_id)[\"body\"] == (\n        \"Enrollment by class:\\n\\n![Fall enrollment by class](image:fall-by-class.png)\\n\\n\"\n        \"Source: IR.\\n\")\n    # And the Editor shows it again from its admin route, with its description.\n    assert img(kind, item_id, \"fall-by-class.png\", \"Fall enrollment by class\") in editor_content(\n        edit_page(analyst, kind, item_id))\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"kind, create, upload\", KINDS)\ndef test_a_description_with_markdown_characters_is_kept_as_typed(analyst, kind, create, upload):\n    item_id = create(analyst)\n    upload(analyst, item_id, png())\n    page = edit_page(analyst, kind, item_id)\n    alt = \"Fall [2025] enrollment *by* class &amp; year\"\n    html = f'<p>{img(kind, item_id, \"fall-by-class.png\", alt)}</p>'\n    save(analyst, kind, item_id, page, body_html=html, body_dirty=\"1\")\n\n    page = edit_page(analyst, kind, item_id)\n    assert img(kind, item_id, \"fall-by-class.png\", alt) in editor_content(page)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"kind, create, upload\", KINDS)\ndef test_changing_a_description_or_removing_an_image_changes_only_that(\n        analyst, kind, create, upload):\n    item_id = create(analyst, body=CHART)\n    upload(analyst, item_id, png())\n    page = edit_page(analyst, kind, item_id)\n    shown = editor_content(page)\n    old = img(kind, item_id, \"fall-by-class.png\", \"Fall enrollment by class\")\n    assert old in shown\n\n    changed = shown.replace(old, img(kind, item_id, \"fall-by-class.png\", \"Students by class, fall 2026\"))\n    assert save(analyst, kind, item_id, page, body_html=changed, body_dirty=\"1\").status_code == 303\n    assert stored(module_for(kind), item_id)[\"body\"] == (\n        \"Enrollment by class:\\n\\n![Students by class, fall 2026](image:fall-by-class.png)\\n\")\n\n    page = edit_page(analyst, kind, item_id)\n    removed = re.sub(r\"<p><img [^>]*></p>\", \"\", editor_content(page))\n    assert save(analyst, kind, item_id, page, body_html=removed, body_dirty=\"1\").status_code == 303\n    assert stored(module_for(kind), item_id)[\"body\"] == \"Enrollment by class:\\n\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"kind, create, upload\", KINDS)\ndef test_an_image_from_anywhere_else_is_left_out(analyst, kind, create, upload):\n    item_id = create(analyst)\n    other = create(analyst, slug=\"other-item\")\n    upload(analyst, other, png())\n    page = edit_page(analyst, kind, item_id)\n    html = (f'<p>Before {img(kind, other, \"fall-by-class.png\", \"Another item\")}'\n            '<img src=\"https://example.test/chart.png\" alt=\"Hot-linked\"> after</p>')\n    save(analyst, kind, item_id, page, body_html=html, body_dirty=\"1\")\n    assert stored(module_for(kind), item_id)[\"body\"] == \"Before after\\n\"\n\n\n# The description: required in the Editor, only warned of by the server.\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"kind, create, upload\", KINDS)\ndef test_an_image_with_no_description_saves_and_is_warned_of(analyst, kind, create, upload):\n    item_id = create(analyst)\n    upload(analyst, item_id, png())\n    page = edit_page(analyst, kind, item_id)\n    html = f'<p>{img(kind, item_id, \"fall-by-class.png\", \"\")}</p>'\n    assert save(analyst, kind, item_id, page, body_html=html, body_dirty=\"1\").status_code == 303\n    assert stored(module_for(kind), item_id)[\"body\"] == \"![](image:fall-by-class.png)\\n\"\n\n    page = edit_page(analyst, kind, item_id)\n    warning = re.search(r'<p class=\"content-image-warning\"[^>]*>(.*?)</p>', page, re.S)\n    assert warning and \"fall-by-class.png\" in warning[1]\n    # It tells the writer how to fix it in the Editor, not in Markdown.\n    assert \"![\" not in warning[1]\n\n\n# The Site preview.\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"kind, create, upload\", KINDS)\ndef test_an_inserted_image_shows_in_the_site_preview_before_it_is_saved(\n              body_dirty=\"1\", item_base=re.search(r'name=\"item_base\" value=\"([^\"]*)\"', page)[1])\n    assert shown.status_code == 200\n    [tag] = img_tags(shown.text)\n    assert If its script doesn't run, the textarea posts Markdown, each\n        part the Editor can't edit standing as its locked-<n> line. #}\n    <div class=\"admin-editor\" data-body-dirty=\"{{ 1 if form.body_dirty else 0 }}\"\n      data-site-items='{{ site_items | tojson }}' data-link-states='{{ link_states | tojson }}'\n      data-chart-preview=\"{{ path_for('preview_chart') }}\">'''\nnew='''        shows the body from the template below, which a browser never renders\n        itself. {"parentUuid":"eddce4f8-1467-46a1-b9d9-91b8af37a64d","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"4dc5332e-fccd-45f6-b53b-fb048524d43a","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_019LSKc4vw6s7JDn3VAwb8ji","type":"tool_result","content":"---\nname: browser-checks-environment\ndescription: \"What works for ticket browser checks here: viewport widths, phone width, real pastes, scratch instance\"\nmetadata:\n  node_type: memory\n  type: reference\n  originSessionId: 6d83085c-4859-4681-9c06-b59afa52f437\n  modified: 2026-10-01T15:44:20.809Z\n---\n\nBrowser checks for closing comments (spec #14) in this environment, as of 2026-10-01:\n\n- **Claude in Chrome's resize_window doesn't change the viewport** (stayed 516 px, or whatever the window is). 768/1440 px checks can't be done that way.\n- **gstack `browse` (headless) is killed by the command sandbox** (exit 137), and running it with the sandbox disabled was refused by the auto-mode classifier. Don't retry; ask the user.\n- **390 px for anything besides the public page** (e.g. a dialog): put a same-origin `<iframe src=\"/admin/...\">` 390 px wide on an admin page and drive it; its `innerWidth` is 390 and media queries apply. {"parentUuid":"74da9847-43eb-4735-b5e3-4cf7ace12ffe","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"4dc5332e-fccd-45f6-b53b-fb048524d43a","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/davelleat/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: since e25c482 — ticket #21 (T18: Chart images in the Editor), spec #14"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"7b82233f-ff5f-488e-8d7b-ee4535a2692c","timestamp":"2026-10-01T16:07:16.851Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01PqZF6iL9jFBdqP9TZMihQF","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"d66c4f2e-a30c-4d8a-a7c5-64b988801fd9","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

Whether that's a bug is a spec question. To move an image already in the body, the old set of images on the page was enough. Adding the panel's thumbnails is what opens this path. Either check the drag in Chrome and Safari, or leave those `src`s out of the list (or set `draggable=false` on the thumbnails).\n  2. **The image goes after the cursor's paragraph, not at the cursor.** The ticket says: \"inserts one at the cursor.\" `applyImage` puts the image in a new paragraph after the block the cursor is in. The Editor also locks that paragraph, which breaks \"Clicking an image in the body lets the writer change its description or remove it\" and \"is stored as `![Description](image:<name>)`\". It is a small fix that the ticket's acceptance criteria need, and it has a direct test.\n    - Side effect: public pages of existing content with escaped alt text now keep those characters in the alt. ADR-005 promises \"existing content [is] unchanged,\" so mention this in the closing comment as an improvement.\n  - **Two other changes are fine.**\n    - The undescribed-image warning now reads \"Click each one in the body and describe…\". The warning is kept, as the ticket asks. Its fix is now written only for the Editor, so it gives no direction to someone using the Markdown textarea when the script fails.\n    - The `CONTEXT.md` Chart image entry follows the spec's Vocabulary section. The admin-only CSS in `public_site.py` is in scope.\n  \n  Nothing else looks like scope creep. Upload, validation, permissions and publishing (ADR-004) are unchanged, and the pasted- and dropped-picture messages now point to \"Insert image\".\n</agent-message>"}

{"parentUuid":"bed6d5b5-7e25-4230-977f-34e2ceeb1fe4","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"24f574ef-6ffc-409d-827b-7c4f806ba2eb","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_015FYNoQYgCupyQTvDMBzBjf","type":"tool_result","content":"## `/code-review` findings (343c201..59ced13)\n\nTwo axes, run separately: **Standards** (CLAUDE.md, SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md, CONTEXT.md, ADR-005/006, CSS naming) and **Spec** (this ticket and spec #14). The fixes are in 5ebed50.\n\n### Standards\n\nNo hard violations. Checks that passed:\n- The preview route has CSRF and login.\n- Every new class has the `admin-editor-chart*` or `admin-chart-builder-*` prefix.\n- No `table`, `th`, or `td` rules sit outside `.content-body`.\n- Every `innerHTML` is either T16's escaped drawing or a constant.\n- `data-chart` is escaped when shown, and parsed again on save.\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| S1 | \"figure\" is an Avoid word in CONTEXT.md, but it was used for a Chart's drawing (the JSON key and a docstring). \"Chart builder\" and \"card\" were new words that weren't in the glossary. | **Fixed.** The preview now answers with `drawing`. CONTEXT.md has a **Chart builder** entry that covers the card. |\n| S2 | `` `${LOCKED}, ${CHART}` `` was repeated 4 times in editor.js. | **Fixed.** It is now one `SHOWN_ONLY` constant. |\n| S3 | `.admin-chart-builder-message` copied `.admin-editor-message`. | **Fixed.** They now share one rule. |\n| S4 | Some names were unclear: `_second`, the inner `check` that shadowed `charts.check`, `shown` used both as a selector and a predicate, and `done`. | **Fixed.** They are now `_first_repeat`, `collect`, `SHOWN_ONLY`/`errorShown`, and `onInsert`. |\n| S5 | Cards go in after nh3, and nothing explained why that's safe. | **Fixed.** `_card_html` now has a comment: the drawing is safe because of how it's built, and the block is escaped and parsed again on save. |\n| S6 | Field paths (`series.N.values.M`) are built by hand in several places, and the JS parses them twice. | **Kept.** The format is fixed, short, and tested end to end through the route. |\n| S7 | `preview_chart` reads the same JSON 3 times (`problems`, `parse`, `suggestion`). | **Kept.** A chart is at most 32 KB, and keeping the three apart keeps each function simple. |\n| S8 | The JS limits (`MOST_CATEGORIES`, `MOST_SERIES`, the number pattern) copy app/charts.py. | **Kept.** The server decides what is valid. The JS copies only size the grid's buttons and tell names from numbers in a paste. The comments say so. |\n| S9 | The preview's `chart` field has no size cap before parsing. | **Kept.** `MAX_BYTES` (32 KB) is checked before parsing, and the route is admin-only. |\n\n### Spec\n\nNothing required is missing.\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| P1 | \"*A paste … fills the grid from the selected cell. The first row and column become names when they aren't numeric.*\" A one-column paste (a series copied with its name) put into a series' name cell overwrote the **category names**, and the name became the axis label. | **Fixed.** A one-column range never counts as category names. Pasted into a series, its non-numeric first cell becomes that series' name. Checked in Chrome: one column into series 1, one into series 2, numbers into a value cell, and the full Sheets range from the browser check. |\n| P2 | A range with names goes to the name row and column wherever it's pasted, not strictly from the selected cell. | **Kept, as approved in the plan.** Names go to the names. A range with no names fills from the selected cell. |\n| P3 | Whole-chart errors (a duplicate, a unit conflict, a category count) show one at a time, and only once every field is right on its own. | **Kept, as approved in the plan.** Each one still shows by its field or cell. |\n| P4 | ADR-006 still said the Editor shows a Chart as a locked block. | **Fixed.** ADR-006 now has a T17 note: a valid top-level Chart is a card, rewritten in canonical form when its body is edited. An invalid or nested Chart is still locked. |\n| P5 | Minor additions nobody asked for: an empty paragraph before or after a leading or trailing locked block or card, a note when a paste was too large, and a \"can't be drawn, reload\" message. | **Kept.** An empty paragraph isn't saved. Without it, a writer can't type after a Chart at the end of the body. |\n\n**Tests:** the full suite passes (1225).\n\n## Browser check (closing)\n\n**Browser:** Google Chrome 154.0.8037.58 on macOS.\n\n**Viewports:**\n- **Desktop:** 1200 × 763 CSS px.\n- **Phone:** a 390 × 740 px same-origin frame holding the edit page. Its own viewport was 390 px wide, checked with `innerWidth`. Resizing the window doesn't change the viewport under this automation.\n\n**Setup:**\n- A throwaway `cms serve` on localhost:8002, with its own seeded database in the session scratchpad. Nothing touched the real `cms.db`.\n- Logged in as the seeded Analyst.\n- Data Bite \"Spring survey response rates\".\n\nScreenshots are under `docs/screenshots/chart-builder-*`.\n\n| Check | Actions | Result |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Typing** | Press **Insert chart**. Type a title. Type `First-year` / `62%` and `Senior` / `48%` into the grid. | **Pass.** The chart is drawn by the server as you type. The empty third row is left out, and Insert becomes enabled. `chart-builder-typing-1200.jpg` |\n| **Not a number** | Type `4x8` in a value cell. | **Pass.** \"'4x8' isn't a number\" appears under the cell, and Insert is disabled. `chart-builder-error-not-a-number.png` |\n| **Other currency** | Type `€48`. | **Pass.** \"'€48' is in a currency other than $\" appears under the cell. `chart-builder-error-currency.png` |\n| **Unit conflict** | Type `$48` among `%` values. | **Pass.** \"'$48' is in $, but the chart's units are %\" appears under the cell. `chart-builder-error-unit-conflict.png` |\n| **Duplicate category** | Type `First-year` twice. | **Pass.** The error appears under the second one. `chart-builder-error-duplicate-category.png` |\n| **Title and Units** | Clear the title. Type `€` in Units. | **Pass.** Each error appears under its own field. `chart-builder-error-title-and-units-1200.jpg` |\n| **Suppressed** | Type `<10`. | **Pass.** It's accepted, no bar is drawn, and the privacy note appears. |\n| **Suggested type** | Type the category `Students living off campus`. | **Pass.** The horizontal-bar suggestion shows, and the type stays Vertical bar. **Use horizontal bar** switches it. `chart-builder-hbar-suggestion-1200.jpg` |\n| **Insert and save** | Press **Insert chart**, then **Save changes**. | **Pass.** A card appears in the body with **Edit chart** and **Remove chart**, and the Site preview follows. The stored body is the canonical `chart` block, read back from the database. `chart-builder-inserted-card-1200.jpg` |\n| **4-series line** (Edit) | Press **Edit chart**. Set Type to Line. Paste a 5 × 6 tab-separated range (names row, years down) into the first category cell. This was a synthetic paste event; the real one is below. | **Pass.** The four series get their names and the years stay as categories. `—` and `*` are accepted, and **Add series** is disabled at 4. The chart has a legend, gaps, \"starts at 82.5%, not zero\" and the privacy note. **Update chart** replaced the card in place. `chart-builder-4-series-line-paste-1200.jpg`, `chart-builder-edited-card-1200.jpg` |\n| **Remove** | Press **Remove chart**, then save. | **Pass.** The card is gone, the Site preview follows, and the stored body has no Chart. `chart-builder-removed-1200.jpg` |\n| **Cancel** | Open the dialog and press **Cancel**. | **Pass.** The dialog closes and the body is untouched (`body_dirty=0`). |\n| **390 px** | Press **Edit chart** at phone width. | **Pass.** The dialog fits (374 px), the preview shows the phone drawing, and the page doesn't scroll sideways. Fixed during the check: the grid's **Remove** buttons were cut off. `chart-builder-dialog-390-top.jpg`, `chart-builder-dialog-390-bottom.jpg` |\n| **Real paste** (by the owner) | Copy a range in **Google Sheets** and paste it into the first category cell. | **Pass, after fixes.** It filled from the cell, with names in the name row and column. Three things looked wrong and were fixed in 59ced13: each series' Remove button pushed the grid's columns out of line, a blank cell's error ran to 3 lines (now \"Can't be blank\"), and the top-left cell (`Class`) was dropped (now the category axis label). `chart-builder-sheets-paste-after-fixes.jpg` |\n\n**Fixed during the check:**\n- The dialog jumped when the chart became invalid. It now keeps the last drawing, faded.\n- Errors next to a cell repeated the cell's location. They now use a short form.\n- The preview was drawn wider than the public column.\n- A body ending in a Chart had no line to type after it.\n\n**Not done:**\n- **Excel.** The real paste was from Google Sheets. {"parentUuid":"0527abec-446a-4034-bfa6-75f9a00a153d","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfboqjZnCw3A2rMxxkcQb","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01C3CzhbDXYDSmx9TuT39XEf","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/d66c4f2e-a30c-4d8a-a7c5-64b988801fd9/scratchpad/t18/review-comment.md","content":"## `/code-review` findings (e25c482..9e78661)\n\nTwo axes, run separately: **Standards** (CLAUDE.md, SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md, CONTEXT.md, CSS naming, and the code around the change) and **Spec** (this ticket and spec #14). The fixes are in REVIEW_SHA.\n\n### Standards\n\nNo hard violations. Checks that passed:\n- No new forms. The image Delete forms keep their CSRF token.\n- `data-images` holds only admin paths, and no `href=\"/…\"` or `src=\"/…\"` reaches `site/`.\n- The new `image_text_join` rule only retypes tokens inside an image's description. It doesn't get around nh3.\n- Every new class has the `admin-editor-image*` prefix, and every element selector is scoped under one.\n- No Avoid words from CONTEXT.md.\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| S1 | In `_edit_page`, `images` was an `ImageLinks`, while `\"images\"` in the template and `images` in editor.js were lists of names or `{name, src}`. | **Fixed.** It is now `links, names`. |\n| S2 | `closeImagePanel` copied `restoreRange()`, which only knew `linkRange`. | **Fixed.** `restoreRange(range = linkRange)` serves both panels. |\n| S3 | The same three lines went into both routes' `_edit_page`. | **Kept.** The two pages were already parallel, and `editing.body_images` holds the shared part. |\n| S4 | `body_images(links, names)` always gets its two arguments together (a data clump). | **Kept.** `ImageLinks` maps names to URLs and back, and listing an item's images belongs to its own module (`data_bites.images`, `reports.images`), which checks who may see them. |\n| S5 | `openImage` had a nested ternary, denser than the code around it. | **Fixed.** Two plain `if`s. |\n| S6 | `openLink` closed the image panel and `openImage` closed the link panel, but `openChart` closed neither. | **Fixed.** Opening the Chart builder closes both, and clears an image's outline. Checked in Chrome. |\n| S7 | `.admin-editor-image-chosen` brought in a new colour, `#0b57d0`. | **Fixed.** It is now `currentColor`, like the chosen thumbnail beside it. |\n\n### Spec\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| P1 | \"*The required description is enforced in the Editor.*\" A thumbnail dragged from the open panel into the body would have stayed, with no description, because drops kept any of the item's image URLs. | **Fixed.** A drop keeps only an image already in the body (a move) or one put there by Insert image. The thumbnails can't be dragged. Checked in Chrome: a dropped thumbnail is removed with the message, and an image moved within the body stays. |\n| P2 | \"*Browser behaviour … is checked by hand in Chrome and Safari.*\" Only Chrome was checked. | **Not done**, as with T15 to T17. It's listed in the closing comment. |\n| P3 | \"*the existing T10/T11 tests still pass*\": three of their assertions were changed. | **Kept, and named here.** They looked for the copy-a-snippet line, which this ticket removes. They now look for the image's name in the \"Chart images\" list: `test_analyst_uploads_an_image_and_the_edit_page_lists_it` (renamed from `…_with_a_snippet`), `test_the_filename_is_sanitized_before_it_names_anything`, and T11's `test_analyst_uploads_to_a_draft_report_and_the_edit_page_lists_it`. Every other T10/T11 test is unchanged and passes. |\n| P4 | \"*inserts one at the cursor*\": the image goes in a paragraph of its own, after the block the cursor is in. | **Kept.** A Chart image is a block, like a table or a Chart, which go in the same way (`placeBlocks`). With the cursor in an empty paragraph, the image takes that paragraph's place. |\n| P5 | The `app/rendering.py` change wasn't on the ticket's list. | **Kept, as needed by the ticket.** markdown-it-py's `text_join` doesn't reach the tokens inside an image's description. So an escaped character there (`\\[`, `\\*`, `\\&`, `&amp;`, which `to_markdown` writes for a description typed in the Editor) was dropped from the alt, and the Editor locked the paragraph. That broke \"*stored as `![Description](image:<name>)`*\" and \"*Clicking an image … change its description*\". Side effect: an existing description with an escape now keeps that character in its alt on the public page, which is a fix. A test covers it. |\n| P6 | The undescribed-image warning now says to click the image in the body. Without the script, that doesn't help. | **Kept.** The Editor is how writers edit. The fallback is for a script that failed. |\n\n**Tests:** the full suite passes (TESTS_COUNT).\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":410,"cache_read_input_tokens":237593,"output_tokens":1925,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":43},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":410,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1925,"cache_read_input_tokens":237593,"cache_creation_input_tokens":410,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":410},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01C3CzhbDXYDSmx9TuT39XEf":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/d66c4f2e-a30c-4d8a-a7c5-64b988801fd9/scratchpad/t18/review-comment.md","content":"## `/code-review` findings (e25c482..9e78661)\n\nTwo axes, run separately: **Standards** (CLAUDE.md, SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md, CONTEXT.md, CSS naming, and the code around the change) and **Spec** (this ticket and spec #14). {"parentUuid":"17187ea2-b141-40e3-a7c8-4426083078ee","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfbp3nS25HCZ35GgZocPe","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"T18 is built, reviewed and checked in Chrome. The closing commit (`1424369`, \"Closes #21\") is local and not pushed, so #21 is still open.\n\n**Pushed without being asked:** I pushed `main` to origin (`e25c482..6676d66`) in the same command that posted the GitHub comments. That covers the first three T18 commits. Only the closing commit is unpushed. Pushing it will close #21; say the word if you want me to.\n\n**What the Editor does now:**\n- **Insert image** lists the item's Chart images with thumbnails. Insert stays disabled until an image is chosen and a description is typed.\n- The image goes into its own paragraph after the one the cursor is in, and is stored as `![Description](image:<name>)`.\n- Clicking an image in the body lets you change its description or remove it.\n- On the create page, the button explains that images can be added after the first save. With no images uploaded yet, it says to upload one first.\n- The copy-a-snippet line is gone from the \"Chart images\" section; each image is listed by name with Delete. The undescribed-image warning stays, now telling the writer to click the image in the body.\n- A pasted or dropped picture is refused with a message pointing to \"Insert image\".\n\n**Bug found and fixed outside the ticket's list:** if a description contained `[`, `*`, `&` or similar, those characters vanished from the alt text on the public page, and the Editor showed that paragraph as uneditable.
